events.title: Frances Allen receives Turing Award
events.summary: Frances Allen became the first woman to win the ACM Turing Award in 2006 for pioneering compiler optimization techniques.
events.about: Allen's work at IBM on automatic parallelization and optimization underpins every modern compiler. She proved deep systems research could come from industry labs, not only academia.

narrative.whyChosen: Allen broke the Turing Award gender barrier for compiler pioneers.
narrative.whyImportant: Her optimizations made high-level languages practical for performance-critical code.
narrative.problemSolved: Early compilers generated naive code; optimization required manual assembly expertise.

events.title: Douglas Crockford popularizes JSON
events.summary: Douglas Crockford specified JSON in 2006 — the data interchange format behind REST APIs and config files.
events.about: JSON replaced XML for most web APIs — simpler for JavaScript clients and human-readable in logs. Crockford's RFC 4627 and json.org made a subset of JavaScript literals the lingua franca of web services.

narrative.whyChosen: JSON became the default API payload format for web and mobile.
narrative.whyImportant: It aligned data exchange with JavaScript object literals.
narrative.problemSolved: XML was verbose and expensive to parse in browsers and mobile clients.
